items.note: Unchanged this run - every ETA and ETD in the rotation matches the 14 Sep record exactly. The AA9 long-term schedule still lists only two voyages, WAN HAI 712 E002 (Port Klang 23 Aug, already in history and out of window) and WAN HAI 903 E002, which is why AA9 stays classified as an extra loader rather than a fixed string: n is 2, not weekly. For contrast the AA7 CSV pulled in the same burst is 2,532 bytes of continuous weekly sailings against 551 bytes for AA9, and AA8 and AA10 return empty 85-byte stubs, so there is no wider AAn programme behind it. The vsProforma comparator is a cross-carrier market benchmark (MSC EMPIRE SERVICE Ningbo to New York, 26 days, departing 19 Sep) rather than a Wan Hai proforma, because Wan Hai's own Ningbo to New York string on AA7 was not sampled on that exact pair this run. Read the +13 day delta as slower than the fastest thing on the water, not as a like-for-like carrier comparison.

items.note: Unchanged and now verified from two independent Maersk surfaces. The vessel-schedule page confirms the Asia legs and the canal call (Gwangyang 19 Sep, Yantian 23 Sep, Busan 28 Sep, Panama Canal 21 Oct) but publishes nothing past the canal; the Houston call comes from the routing API, which returns estimatedTimeOfArrival 2026-10-31T09:00 at USHOUTM (Barbours Cut). Both the Yantian and Busan lanes return exactly one XL sailing against six or seven TP15 sailings, so n is 1 on each. Delta is the same +8 days on both pairs: Yantian XL 38d against TP15 SAN FERNANDO 635E 30d, Busan XL 33d against the same TP15 sailing at 25d. WARNING FOR FUTURE RUNS: the routing API field isRoutingAdhoc is true on every routing returned for these lanes, including the plain proforma TP15 sailings. It is not an ad-hoc signal and must never be used as a trigger - the only thing separating this item from the rest of the lane is the serviceName XL sitting outside the registry.

alerts.message: OGEC / EVER LASTING 0021-097E rotation slipped. BEFORE (14 Sep run): Shanghai ETD 13 Sep, Ningbo ETD 15 Sep, New York ETA 15 Oct, Ningbo to NY 30 days. AFTER (16 Sep run): Shanghai ETD 16 Sep, Ningbo ETD 20 Sep, New York ETA 16 Oct, Ningbo to NY 26 days. Savannah ETA moved 20 Oct to 21 Oct. Asia departures pushed 3 to 5 days later, US arrivals moved 1 day, so the quoted transits shortened by up to 4 days. All in-window departures still fall inside weeks 38 and 39.

AUG appears on Evergreen's US Gulf lanes and is in neither the registry nor the deny-list: Yantian to Houston n=3 (CONTI CORTESIA 014E 16 Sep, ONE ARCADIA 079E 01 Oct, EVER LUCKY 085E 05 Oct), Ningbo to Houston n=4, Shanghai to Houston n=1 (EVER LUCKY 085E 11 Oct). n is 3 or more on two separate lanes, the sailings are roughly weekly, and the tonnage spans at least two carriers (Evergreen and ONE), so this reads as a fixed Asia to US Gulf proforma string, not an extra loader. Not published as an XL. Per the detection rule it is flagged now and should be promoted into the Ocean Alliance registry block once a second run confirms it.

Maersk's routing API exposes isRoutingAdhoc and it returned true for every single routing on both Yantian to Houston and Busan to Houston, including the ordinary proforma TP15 sailings. Treat it exactly like Hapag's isGemini: context only, never a trigger. If a future run starts flagging TP15, the isRoutingAdhoc handling has regressed.

Regression fixtures pass. Hapag Yantian to New York returned AA7 5 with isGemini false and US4 6 with isGemini true and nothing was flagged, which is the expected result. Evergreen Shanghai to New York returned SAX 4, NUE2 4, CBX 3, NUE 3 and OGEC 1, and only OGEC was flagged. Evergreen Yantian to New York returned SAX 3, AUE 3, CBX 4 and no OGEC this run - the Yantian OGEC call belonged to the TRITON voyage, which is now historic, confirming that rotations must be worked up per voyage and never inherited from a previous sighting of the same code.

The documented ShipmentLink seed-then-replay dance was not needed this run and the origin autocomplete panel never rendered in the background tab. Reading frmSubmit shows it only copies tvs2OriAC_hideValue and tvs2DesAC_hideValue into oriLocation and desLocation, sets departureDateShow, and calls document.routing.submit(). Setting both hidden fields programmatically and then calling frmSubmit works, as long as groupRadioOri and groupRadioDes stay on their default ALL - the East/West USCA checkbox validation only fires when a coast radio is selected. Thirteen Evergreen lanes were swept this way without a single real click.
